rationale: C03 is a highly plausible material drafting template. Both proclamations use the same Article XIX safeguard mechanism and nearly the same sequence: identify existing GATT concessions and customs treatment; recite a Tariff Commission section 7 investigation finding increased imports and serious injury; find that modified concessions and new customs treatment are necessary; invoke section 350, section 7(c), and Article XIX; then modify specified Schedule XX items and prescribe their application until otherwise proclaimed. The child adapts this concrete framework from metal articles and quantitative quotas to stainless-steel flatware and a tariff-rate quota. C10 and C22 contain related quota or safeguard machinery, but their language and overall operative sequence are less closely matched.

shared_material.child_excerpt: the Commission has found that, as a result in part of the duties reflecting the concessions... [the products] were being imported... in such increased quantities, both actual and relative, as to cause serious injury to the domestic industry producing like products
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the Commission has found that the articles... are, as a result in part of the customs treatment... being imported... in such increased quantities, both actual and relative, as to cause serious injury to the domestic industries producing like or directly competitive products
shared_material.explanation: Distinctive, closely parallel statement of the Tariff Commission's safeguard finding.

shared_material.child_excerpt: I find that in order to remedy the serious injury to the domestic industry it is necessary that there be applied... the customs treatment hereinafter proclaimed
shared_material.parent_excerpt: I find that the modifications of the concessions... to permit the application to such articles of the customs treatment hereinafter proclaimed is necessary to remedy the serious injury
shared_material.explanation: The child closely adapts C03's finding that changed customs treatment is necessary to remedy serious injury.

shared_material.child_excerpt: section 350... authorizes the President to proclaim such modifications of existing duties and such additional import restrictions as are required or appropriate to carry out any foreign trade agreement
shared_material.parent_excerpt: the said section 350... authorizes the President to proclaim such modifications of existing duties and such additional import restrictions as are required or appropriate to carry out any foreign trade agreement
shared_material.explanation: Substantially identical legal-authority recital within the same distinctive safeguard sequence.

shared_material.child_excerpt: acting under the authority vested in me by section 350... and by section 7(c)... and in accordance with the provisions of Article XIX... do proclaim that... (a) the said prevailing tariff concessions... are hereby modified
shared_material.parent_excerpt: acting under the authority vested in me by section 350... and by section 7(c)... and in accordance with the provisions of Article XIX... do proclaim as follows: (a) Item 391... item 393, and item 394... shall each be modified
shared_material.explanation: Nearly identical authority clause followed by the same operative act of modifying enumerated tariff-schedule concessions.

shared_material.child_excerpt: The provisions of the proviso... added by paragraph (a) above, shall be applied and all proclamations... are suspended insofar as they are inconsistent with this proclamation.
shared_material.parent_excerpt: The articles described in the said items... shall be subject to the quantitative limitations specified in the said items, as modified by paragraph (a) above
shared_material.explanation: Both use a two-part operative structure: paragraph (a) modifies tariff-schedule text and paragraph (b) directs application of the newly modified treatment.
